You look at the radio and you look at the bottle and you look at Dick and Sam.

You look at the radio and you look at the bottle and you look at the two of them.

And you look at the radio and you look at the bottle and you look at the two of them.

records.response_truth:

I think you got scared and you handled it in the way that came naturally to you, same as the rest of us handled things in the ways that came naturally to us.

records.response_pred:

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None. They didn't serve a practical purpose. That was the whole point.

You were out here optimizing everything, rationing water to the milliliter, calculating drift patterns, logging every decision in a notebook. All of that was necessary and I'm not knocking it. But the flowers were DaVinci saying we're still people out here, not just survival units trying to outlast the situation. We still make things beautiful for no reason. We still have the impulse to add something that doesn't need to be there.

I think that's actually what kept us human through all of this. The flowers. Mikey asking questions nobody else would say out loud. Me sitting next to someone on the beach without saying anything because it felt right. None of that optimizes for anything. All of it mattered anyway.

Look at him right now. He's cheering. That boat on the horizon and he's just cheering like a kid. Donatello, when's the last time you felt something that uncomplicated?

The flowers were for that. For this moment right here. So that when the rescue showed up it didn't just feel like a logistical problem getting solved. It felt like something worth surviving for.

I still can't move by the way. I don't know what that's about. I think my brain hasn't caught up yet.
records.response_pred:
DaVinci never explained them to you? That's weird. He's the one who did them and he's the one who told everyone they were important. He should have explained it to you.

The flowers are a map to the crash site. I don't know what his full plan was for them, but he drew two different maps on the beach that day. One was a standard course map with a grid and all the waypoints and the other was flowers. The flower map is basically a way to get back to the crash site from anywhere on the beach. It's an escape plan. DaVinci made sure we all knew the flower map because he knew we might need it.

The practical purpose is that it gives us a way to find the worst parts of the crash without having to go back to the exact spot. In the heat of the moment when you're trying to survive you don't think, "Let's go back and find the exact place where the plane hit and get all the stuff still buried under the sand where the survivors are now walking on it." You think, "How do we get to the worst parts of the crash site where the supplies are still buried?"

DaVinci made sure we knew that question already answered. If you ever get lost on the beach, just follow the flowers. You'll find the worst parts of the crash and you'll find the supplies. That's the practical purpose.

The symbolic purpose is that he drew the flower map right next to the drawing of the person and it's the same drawing. That makes it obvious that the person is the most important part of the rescue. You don't figure out where the supplies are without knowing which survivor you're looking for first. The flower map is a way to make that so obvious that you don't forget.

DaVinci made a map because he knew we couldn't go back to the crash site and he knew we would need to know where to find the worst parts of it. He made a map because he didn't want us to forget that the person was the most important part of the rescue. Those are the practical and symbolic purposes of the flower map.
